findings.impact: An invalid entry (e.g. target_release=v1.2.0) can be merged to main via a rule-deprecate PR, pass the schema validation step at every subsequent workflow run, and accumulate silently in the register until the next tag-cut attempt. The runtime ramp-check catches it before a bad tag is cut, so no tag is ever cut with an invalid entry — but the schema does not provide early detection at PR time. Operators reading only the schema (e.g. while authoring a new deprecation entry) receive no guidance that target_release must be vX.0.0.
findings.mitigation: Two-part fix. (A) Tighten schema pattern: change target_release `pattern` from `^v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$` to `^v[0-9]+\\.0\\.0$`. (B) Update the target_release field description to add: 'Must be a MAJOR release (vX.0.0) per policies/VERSIONING.md — the MAJOR bump is the breaking-change vehicle; the release-gate workflow refuses any entry where MINOR or PATCH is non-zero.' These changes make the schema self-documenting and provide defense-in-depth at the schema-validation step rather than relying solely on the ramp-check step. Alternatively file as TF-020H3rg-004 if deferred; risk is low since runtime enforcement catches it before any tag is cut.

findings.claim: ADOPT-001 §12.7.7 SCP-EREL-001 row Adopter-side relevance cell says 'the deprecation `::warning::` annotations on rule denies' — the phrase 'on rule denies' mischaracterizes the SCP-DEP-001 annotation class in the adjacent row, which covers 'a rule (or other public surface) in its one-MINOR ramp window' and fires regardless of the rule's deny/warn threshold setting.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.7 line 980 (SCP-EREL-001 row Adopter-side relevance): 'Adopters interact with the same invariants via SCP-E007 (rule-config schema/expiry at PR time) + the deprecation `::warning::` annotations on rule denies.' ADOPT-001 §12.7.7 line 981 (SCP-DEP-001 row): 'Per-PR deprecation `::warning::` annotation emitted while a rule (or other public surface) is in its one-MINOR ramp window before removal at the next MAJOR.' VERSIONING.md lines 208-209: 'The rule's own Rego implementation emits a per-PR ::warning::... annotation.' VERSIONING.md lines 224-229: 'Non-rule surfaces (workflow inputs, schema fields, annotation titles, branch-protection helper flags, tag-protection patterns) follow the same ramp pattern with surface-specific emission paths.' A rule at `threshold: warn` would emit the deprecation ::warning:: during the ramp window even though no deny fires; the SCP-EREL-001 row's 'on rule denies' implies the warning is paired only with denies.
findings.impact: Adopter reading SCP-EREL-001 row's Adopter-side relevance description gets an imprecise picture of when SCP-DEP-001 fires: they may expect the deprecation warning only on deny-firing rules (threshold: deny) and miss it on warn-threshold deprecated rules or on non-rule surface deprecations. Minor confusion risk; no governance gap in enforcement.
findings.mitigation: In SCP-EREL-001 Adopter-side relevance cell, replace 'the deprecation `::warning::` annotations on rule denies' with 'the per-surface deprecation `::warning::` annotations (SCP-DEP-001) emitted during the one-MINOR ramp window' — this matches the SCP-DEP-001 row definition and accurately scopes the annotation class across both rule and non-rule surfaces regardless of deny/warn threshold.

The `continue` after appending skips the ramp check for the malformed entry, preventing a spurious second violation from the ramp logic.

positive_verifications.detail: VERSIONING.md reads coherently top-to-bottom: Semver guarantee table → What counts as breaking → What does NOT → Deprecation ramp (one-release warning window + machine enforcement subsection with both modes) → Tag-cut procedure (4-step mandatory pre-flight) → Bad-tag recovery procedure (immutable tag + corrected v<X>.<Y+1>.0 path) → What stable means → Adopter actions → How to file amending decision → References. All 11 rows are internally consistent. DISPATCH-NOTE: Architectural framing section added; Out-of-scope section restructured with named TFs and not-needed list. No contradictions across the three documents.

TF-020H3rg-001 proposes 'a future linter step in policy-check.yml (or a separate workflow) that greps for new deprecated warning emissions in a PR diff and refuses if no corresponding policies/deprecations.yaml entry was added in the same PR.' This follows the existing pattern: policy-check.yml already has multiple linter/validation steps; the step would use git diff to inspect the PR's changed files; refusing on condition (deprecated warning added but no deprecations.yaml entry) is a well-established pattern in GitHub Actions. The step does not require any new infrastructure beyond the existing pyyaml + jsonschema + bash already present in the workflow. No deadline is specified (forward-compat), which is appropriate given no deprecations are currently announced and the step would only trigger when the first rule-RFC deprecation proposal is filed. The closure path is specific and actionable.

The release-gate workflow (020H.3) closes two tracked-forward items: TF-005 (deferred from 020C.1, plan §4) and TF-020H1-001 (deferred from 020H.1). Both closures are tracked in STATUS.md and do not change the plan's architectural intent. No new plan element is introduced by 020H.3 — the workflow is the machine implementation of D-036's already-ratified deprecation ramp clause. The Post-Threshold-A backlog in STATUS.md covers 020H.3 as an extension of the existing Threshold-A work without requiring a plan §3 sequence change. docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020H sub-items are satisfied by the 020H.x slices without requiring §3 resequencing.
